The linear algebra notes are split across these pages:

- [Vectors](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd):
  column vectors, transposes, linear combinations, special vectors, and orthogonality.
- [Matrices](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd):
  matrices, their [rows](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-row) and [columns](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-column),
  transposes, addition, and [scalar multiplication](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-scalar-mult).
- The [Matrix Multiplication](linear-algebra-matrix-multiplication.qmd) page:
  [matrix products](linear-algebra-matrix-multiplication.qmd#def-matrix-mult),
  [square matrices](linear-algebra-matrix-multiplication.qmd#def-square-matrix), [identity matrices](linear-algebra-matrix-multiplication.qmd#def-identity-matrix),
  [matrix-vector products](linear-algebra-matrix-multiplication.qmd#def-matvec-mult),
  and the transpose rules for addition and multiplication.
- The [Linear and Affine Maps](linear-algebra-linear-maps.qmd) page:
  linear and affine maps, and [hyperplanes](linear-algebra-linear-maps.qmd#def-hyperplane).
  <!-- no-figure: an overview list of page topics, and the hyperplane figures are on the linked page -->
- [Subspaces and Rank](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd):
  rank, subspaces, and bases.
- The [Column Space and Null Space](linear-algebra-column-null-space.qmd) page:
  column, row and null spaces of a matrix,
  and [Gram matrices](linear-algebra-column-null-space.qmd#def-gram-matrix).
- The [Rank-Nullity and Rank Factorization](linear-algebra-rank-nullity.qmd) page:
  [rank-nullity](linear-algebra-rank-nullity.qmd#thm-rank-nullity),
  the rank of matrix products, and rank factorization.
- The [Affine Subspaces and Half-Spaces](linear-algebra-affine-subspaces.qmd) page:
  affine subspaces, hyperplanes, and half-spaces.
- [Direct Sums and Orthogonal Complements](linear-algebra-direct-sums.qmd):
  sums and direct sums, orthogonal complements,
  and the fundamental theorem of linear algebra.
- [Inner Products and Orthogonality](linear-algebra-inner-products.qmd):
  inner products, the Cauchy-Schwarz and triangle inequalities, norms, angles,
  Gram-Schmidt, and outer products.
- The [Special Matrices, Quadratic Forms and Trace](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd) page:
  symmetric, diagonal, inverse, projection and orthogonal matrices,
  quadratic forms, the trace, and the [matrix inner product](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-inner-product).
- The [Eigenvalues and Matrix Decompositions](linear-algebra-decompositions.qmd) page:
  eigenvalues, the spectral theorem, [eigendecompositions](linear-algebra-decompositions.qmd#def-eigendecomposition) and the SVD.
- The [Definite Matrices and Determinants](linear-algebra-definite-matrices.qmd) page:
  [positive definite](linear-algebra-definite-matrices.qmd#def-positive-definite) and semidefinite matrices,
  [condition numbers](linear-algebra-definite-matrices.qmd#def-condition-number),
  [matrix-induced inner products](linear-algebra-definite-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-induced-inner-product), and determinants.
- [Design Matrices and Projections](linear-algebra-projections.qmd):
  design matrices, the [hat matrix](linear-algebra-projections.qmd#def-hat-matrix) and [orthogonal projection](linear-algebra-projections.qmd#def-orthogonal-projection).
- [Generalized Inverses and Linear Systems](linear-algebra-generalized-inverses.qmd):
  generalized inverses, the [Moore-Penrose inverse](linear-algebra-generalized-inverses.qmd#def-moore-penrose),
  and when a linear system has a solution.
- [Solving Linear Systems and Least Squares](linear-algebra-least-squares.qmd):
  back substitution, the QR factorization, the [LU factorization](linear-algebra-least-squares.qmd#def-lu),
  least squares and the [normal equations](linear-algebra-least-squares.qmd#def-normal-equations).
- [Diagonalization and Cholesky](linear-algebra-diagonalization.qmd):
  similarity, diagonalization, Schur complements, and the Cholesky factorization.
- [Complex Vectors and Matrices](linear-algebra-complex.qmd):
  conjugate transposes and Hermitian matrices.

A link to a section, theorem or definition on this page from before the split
goes on to the page that now holds it.

# Further reading {#sec-additional-resources}

- @strang2023linear
  is a widely used first course in linear algebra.
  It covers vectors, elimination, vector spaces, orthogonality, determinants,
  eigenvalues, and the singular value decomposition.
- @nield2022essential
  is a short, code-driven introduction to the linear algebra used in data science (Chapter 4).
- @axler2024linear
  is a proof-based treatment centered on vector spaces and linear maps.
  A free electronic version is available from the publisher.
- @lange2010numerical
  covers computing [eigenvalues](linear-algebra-decompositions.qmd#def-eigenvalue) and [eigenvectors](linear-algebra-decompositions.qmd#def-eigenvector),
  including Jacobi's method (Chapter 8),
  and the singular value decomposition, its properties, and its applications (Chapter 9).
- @fieller2018basics
- @banerjee2014linear
- @searle2017matrix
- @petersen2012matrix
  is a free desk reference that collects matrix identities:
  it lists results on determinants, inverses, decompositions,
  and [derivatives](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-derivative) of vectors and matrices,
  so it is a quick place to look up a formula these pages prove.
- @stanford2024ee278notes
  (Stanford EE 278, taught by Tsachy Weissman) applies this page's tools to probability and inference.
  Its "MMSE Geometry" lecture treats the best estimate as an orthogonal [projection](linear-algebra-projections.qmd),
  and its lectures on spectral decomposition, the Karhunen-Loeve expansion and principal component analysis
  treat [diagonalization](linear-algebra-diagonalization.qmd) of a covariance matrix.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLZHQObOWTQDPD3MizzM2xVFitgF8hE_ab)
  is a 16-video YouTube playlist by Grant Sanderson (3Blue1Brown) that develops visual and geometric intuition for vectors, linear combinations, spans, linear transformations, matrix multiplication, determinants, inverses, dot and cross products, change of basis, and eigenvectors and eigenvalues.
